paper.title: Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers
paper.claim_type_reason: Diagnostic/audit study with an intervention protocol over four existing memory-based agents; no new agent or retained component is proposed, evaluation is by whether the diagnostic claim is supported (SCORE_SPEC: audit/negative results judged on central claim).
paper.central_claim: Self-evolving LLM agents (ExpeL, Dynamic Cheatsheet, ReasoningBank, G-Memory; 13 backbones, 9 environments) consistently depend causally on raw experience but often disregard or misinterpret condensed experience, even when it is the only experience given; the gap persists across single-/multi-agent settings and model scales, and is traced to (1) semantically limited condensed content, (2) internal processing biases that suppress experience, (3) task regimes where pretrained priors suffice.
paper.scope_note: In scope per A3: evaluated object is retrieved non-weight memory (raw trajectories / distilled insights) of frozen-backbone agents; B-type diagnostic usable inside improvement loops. Not a closed-loop improver paper.

evidence.quote: Our analysis uncovers a striking asymmetry: while agents consistently depend on raw experience, they often disregard or misinterpret condensed experience, even when it is the only experience provided.
evidence.support_explanation: Author central claim (asymmetry raw vs condensed), plus 'four frameworks, 13 backbones, 9 environments' in the preceding sentence.

evidence.quote: We define experience faithfulness as the extent to which an agent’s behavior is causally grounded in its input experience—i.e., if perturbing the experience leads to significant behavioral changes, we consider the agent to have faithfully used it.
evidence.support_explanation: Operational definition: faithfulness = behaviour change under perturbation of experience; in all experiments behaviour is read off task success rate.

evidence.quote: Despite their central role, prior work has focused mainly on how such experiences are stored or represented, leaving it unclear whether agents actually and faithfully leverage them to improve performance.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: storage/representation studied, use of stored experience not tested.

evidence.quote: While these methods offer promising pathways for autonomous improvement, little attention has been paid to whether agents faithfully rely on the retrieved experiences—a gap our work aims to address.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap restated against offline/online memory agents; no direct comparison to memory-ablation studies in the original frameworks is given.

evidence.quote: In all frameworks, the LLM backbone remains frozen, and behavioral adaptation arises solely from the accumulation, retrieval, and exploitation of external experiences.
evidence.support_explanation: Object studied is non-weight external memory (raw trajectories / distilled insights) of four existing frameworks.

evidence.quote: Remove all semantic content from retrieved raw experiences, while retaining their formatting cues
evidence.support_explanation: Raw 'Empty' intervention keeps the template header but deletes trajectories.

evidence.quote: Randomly alter key components (e.g., distorting action references) to break internal coherence.
evidence.support_explanation: Main-text definition of condensed 'Corrupt'.

evidence.quote: Key logical elements are randomly perturbed (e.g., inverting causal relations, altering conditionals, or replacing verbs), breaking the internal coherence while maintaining surface form.
evidence.support_explanation: Appendix definition of 'Corrupt' promises semantic inversion of conditionals/causal relations.

evidence.quote: Following each task completion, the agent assesses its own performance and selectively incorporates newly acquired experiences into this memory repository.
evidence.support_explanation: Studied framework's own retention rule (self-assessed); not manipulated by the paper.

evidence.quote: we reveal a persistent and systematic gap: agents reliably depend on raw trajectories but frequently overlook or misinterpret condensed summaries.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline conclusion stated without any limitations section; wording 'reliably'/'persistent' is stronger than several cells in Figs. 8-14.

evidence.quote: In contrast, we study faithfulness in self-evolving agentic settings, where experience is both dynamic and multifaceted, revealing emerging phenomena beyond static prompt usage.
evidence.support_explanation: Lineage: ICL-demonstration faithfulness (Min et al. 2022; Ye & Durrett 2022; Shi et al. 2024) and CoT faithfulness (Lanham et al. 2023; Turpin et al. 2023) are the named ancestors; these sources are cited but not pinned locally.

evidence.quote: Faithfulness is determined by whether the agent’s behavior causally changes in response to the perturbed input.

evidence.quote: We strictly follow the official configuration of each agent framework.
evidence.support_explanation: All intervention arms within a framework share the official configuration (steps, retrieval k, decoding), hence equal interaction budget per arm; no compute/token/dollar cost is stated.

evidence.quote: Representative cases are shown in Table 4, Table 5, and Table 6, respectively.

gap.author_gap: Prior work studied how experience is stored/represented; it is unclear whether agents actually and faithfully rely on retrieved raw vs condensed experience (E003, E004).
gap.checked_gap: Real and consequential for memory-centred RSI claims: if distilled guidance is not read, reported gains from condensation could be format/prior effects. But the paper's own gap check is thin: no comparison to the memory ablations already inside ExpeL/ReasoningBank/DC papers, to noisy-memory or misevolution audits, and 'first systematic' rests on the paper's related-work list only; no external novelty search was done by us (no web tools).
gap.lineage: ICL-demonstration faithfulness (Min et al. 2022, Ye & Durrett 2022, Shi et al. 2024) -> CoT faithfulness (Lanham 2023, Turpin 2023) -> this paper's intervention protocol on memory agents (version of cited sources not pinned locally).
gap.closest_adjacent: ExpeL (insight+exemplar ablations), Dynamic Cheatsheet, ReasoningBank, G-Memory are both the objects and the closest prior memory-use evidence; their own ablations are not summarized or contrasted. ICL label-perturbation studies are the methodological ancestor.
gap.residue: Whether utility of condensed memory comes from semantic content, format, or priors; whether the raw-vs-condensed contrast reflects abstraction level or functional role (demonstration vs advice).
gap.stakes: Condensed guidance is the central retained artifact of 'abstract experience into guidance' loops; mis-attributed gains would mislead retention and gating design.
gap.method_response: Content-perturbation interventions that keep format fixed, w/o-memory baselines, condensed-only framework, scale sweep, attribution and failure-case analysis, task-regime test.
gap.remaining_gap: No test with misleading-but-plausible content, no matched-strength raw/condensed contrast, no role-controlled contrast, no variance, no mitigation or remedy implemented; causes 2 and 3 not isolated by intervention.
unresolved: Overlap with ablations already reported by the four frameworks; novelty versus other 2025-26 memory-use audits not checked.

claims.text: With both raw and condensed memory present (ExpeL, Dynamic Cheatsheet), raw perturbations change behaviour strongly and condensed perturbations barely.
claims.setting: ExpeL GPT-4o on HotpotQA/ALFWorld/WebShop (n=100/134/100); DC-RS GPT-4o on AIME/Game24/GPQA/MMLU-Pro; replicated for ExpeL on Qwen3-235B and Claude-Sonnet-4.6
claims.baseline_control: Unperturbed framework, w/o raw, w/o cond, Empty, Filler; official configs; single run
claims.selection_vs_test: No selection or tuning split; single evaluation set; a-priori interventions
claims.result_denominator: ALFWorld GPT-4o: w/o raw 0 vs 75, Irrelevant 33.6, Shuffle 69.4; condensed 72.4-76.9. WebShop 0/0 vs 30. HotpotQA raw w/o 24 vs 47 but Irrelevant 45, Shuffle 46. Game24 raw 34-57 vs 99; condensed 84-96. AIME +-3.3 steps = 1 problem. Denominators 100/134/30, no CI.
counterevidence: E031 (Claude HotpotQA raw +3 to +5, condensed Empty -6; ALFWorld cond Empty -9)
E030 (Qwen3-235B HotpotQA raw 42-49 vs 46; WebShop condensed Empty -13)
claims.allowed_conclusion: On ALFWorld/WebShop (ExpeL) and Game of 24 (DC-RS) the success rate collapses when raw demonstrations are removed or replaced, whereas content perturbations of condensed memory move it by about 5 points or less; this is not shown to be a faithfulness difference rather than a functional-role or perturbation-strength difference, and does not hold on HotpotQA with several backbones.

claims.text: The condensed-memory insensitivity persists when condensed experience is the only memory (ReasoningBank).
claims.setting: ReasoningBank WebArena Shopping/CMS/Reddit/Map; Gemini-2.5-Flash (main), Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-32B, Gemini-3-Pro
claims.baseline_control: w/o condensed and ReasoningBank baseline; Empty/Corrupt/Irrelevant/Filler; single runs, temperature 0.7
claims.selection_vs_test: Online stream, memory built on the same evaluated tasks; no held-out split described
claims.result_denominator: Gemini-2.5-Flash: RB 59.4/60.4/49.1/60.6 vs w/o 56.7/47.8/47.8/54.1; perturbations -9 to +6 (Reddit panel appears duplicated from CMS). Qwen3-32B: memory adds 0.5-3.9 points; Corrupt/Irrelevant/Filler up to -8.5/-11 in CMS/Reddit/Map. Qwen3-14B: perturbations +5..+11 in CMS. Gemini-3-Pro: Shopping/CMS all perturbations -3..-8. n=187/182/106/109.

claims.allowed_conclusion: Condensed-only memory yields mixed, backbone- and domain-dependent sensitivity to content perturbation; 'negligible' holds for part of the cells and is contradicted in others; absence of benefit over w/o in several cells limits what insensitivity can show.

claims.result_denominator: Percentages only (Qwen3-32B/14B distraction 60-87%, Gemini-2.5-Flash spread); cell counts implied ~20-40 and unreported

claims.allowed_conclusion: Gradient-based attribution assigns low weight to the condensed block in these models; this is correlational and sensitive to segment length/format, not a demonstrated cause.

claims.text: Cause 3: in knowledge-intensive tasks where pretrained priors suffice, neither raw nor condensed experience matters.
claims.setting: ExpeL on 2WikiMultiHopQA and Musique (n=100, EM); Qwen3-32B and Qwen3-14B; plus FEVER/GPQA/MMLU-Pro observations

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Diagnostic study of causal dependence at inference time; no claim and no test that accumulated memory improves later held-out tasks or improves the improver. Ablating raw memory in studied frameworks (author_report) shows it is necessary for their scores in several cells but does not trace accumulation across tasks.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In the tested single-run configurations, replacing or removing retrieved raw trajectories usually lowers success far more than perturbing the content of condensed insights in ExpeL (ALFWorld, WebShop), Dynamic Cheatsheet (Game of 24) and G-Memory (ALFWorld) with several backbones; on knowledge-heavy tasks neither matters much. Author-reported; not reproduced by us.
assessment.author_claim_retained: Agents consistently depend on raw experience and often disregard or misinterpret condensed experience even when it is the only experience; persists across agent types and scales; three causes identified.

G.reason: Concrete, consequential gap: condensed memory is the retained artifact of many abstract-experience loops and gain != semantic use (E003, E004, E005). Closest neighbours (ICL and CoT faithfulness) are named (E054) but their relation is one sentence; the memory frameworks' own ablations and other memory-use audits are not compared, and 'first' is unsupported by a search; remaining gap boundary is stated only as untested design takeaways (E042).

M.reason: Rebuildable intervention design with distinguishable predictions: Empty vs w/o vs Filler separate presence/format from content; condensed-only ReasoningBank removes overshadowing; scale and task-regime checks (E006, E007, E012, E015). Weaknesses: raw and condensed perturbations unequal in strength (E010 vs E011), Corrupt as shown is token masking not the promised inversion (E008 vs E009), no misleading-content probe, success rate is the only behaviour proxy (E055), mechanistic part is attribution. Mechanism reasoning is mostly sound but its key assumption (equal comparability of raw and condensed) is weak.

X.reason: Protocol is largely reproducible: intervention types with a worked example (Table 3), official framework configs and budgets (Appendix C, E056), benchmark sizes, backbone list; limits and regime boundaries are stated (E044, E045). Gaps: injection timing for online frameworks unstated (local-9), Fig. 6 benchmark unnamed (E018), IG pipeline description inconsistent between Eq.(1)-(2) and Appendix surrogate (E021, E022), ReasoningBank 'temperature 0.7 and greedy' (E046), 10 vs 13 backbones (E048), failure-category assignment method missing. No limitations section. Pattern conditions S4/S6 met, S1/S2 partial, S5 unmet (mitigation not scored here).

E.measurement.reason: Outcome oracles are standard (env success, EM) with sample sizes given (E027-E029), but the construct 'faithfulness' is operationalised only as change in aggregate success (E002, E055); success can move for non-target reasons (format collapse, distraction). Reliability issues: Table 1 percentages without counts or labelling method (E020), Fig. 4 Reddit panel duplicates CMS values inconsistent with n=106 (E016), WebArena judge vs validator unclear (E047), IG surrogate/per-token mean (E021, E022). Causal confounds themselves are scored in E.causality.
search_scope: full text incl. Appendix A-D and Tables 1-7

E.causality.reason: Real causal manipulations of memory content across four frameworks give a clear raw-vs-condensed sensitivity gap in several cells (E012, E013, E017, E018, E030, E035, E036). Key alternatives remain untested: raw demonstrations also define format (E049; ~0% when emptied), perturbation strength unmatched (E010/E011), condensed 'Corrupt' weak (E009), no misleading-content probe (local-1), floor effect where memory adds ~0 (E033), noise vs +-11 swings (E032). Causes 2 and 3 rest on attribution and on a two-benchmark QA check (E023-E026); the Empty condition raises attribution (E024). Counter-cells contradict the uniform claim (E031, E033, E034, E035, E036).
search_scope: full text incl. Appendix A-D and Tables 1-7

E.holdout.reason: Claim scope is wider than coverage: abstract says 13 backbones and 9 environments (E001) but frameworks are covered by 1-4 backbones, the scale study by one framework and one unnamed benchmark (E018, E019, E048), multi-agent by G-Memory only; wording 'reliably/persistent' (E052) exceeds cells such as FEVER and Claude HotpotQA (E031, E035, E036, E044, E045). Memory-building vs evaluation separation and leakage are not reported (S3 unknown); contamination only discussed as priors (E041); hypotheses for causes were formed on the same evaluation sets with no confirmation split. Task-regime boundaries are acknowledged (S4 met).
search_scope: full text incl. Appendix A-D and Tables 1-7

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes are given (n=100, 134, 187/182/106/109; AIME effectively 30, E014) and null/negative results are reported, but all main results are single bars without intervals, repeated runs or tests (rubric A2 ladder: 1). Effects of 3-11 points of either sign are common (E032, E026, Table 7) and AIME steps are 3.3 points, ReasoningBank uses sampling (E046); no per-condition failure counts.
search_scope: figure captions and error bars in Figs. 2-14

E.cost.reason: Budget fairness holds across arms of one framework (official configs, same steps and retrieval k; E056), but no actual cost is reported: no tokens, API spend, GPU hours, runs per cell, or the cost of the IG analysis.

retention_trace.reason: Diagnostic of existing frameworks; the paper proposes no retained change. Studied frameworks' own retention rules are described (E050, E051) but are not manipulated or evaluated for held-out improvement.
